inputs.name: finite-window count
inputs.cite: M-201 (Day's Q36 inputs: mu L = 30, T = 252,000)

day.reading: k = mu is a steady-state identity; no finite period has k = mu under overlap except a static N_e equal to census; it has no time term, so it cannot bound a window
day.holds: from an empty start the window count is below mu L T at every finite T (84.1% at N_e = 1e4, 20% at T = 4 N_e, M-201); census fluctuation with overlap moves k over a window (M-210); Day's own Z22903977 says a count needs assumptions the identity cannot supply

critic.reading: k = mu is the expected long-run substitution rate; the cited paper is outside evolution journals and gives no derivation of the claim; Hancock: refuted by 1930s theory
critic.holds: the cited paper has no mutation, so it cannot show k != mu (B1e: relevant to P_fix(t), not to k vs mu); from an equilibrium start the window count is mu L T at every T (M-201); k/mu = 1 at any constant N/N_e (M-209), so 'equal to census' is not a condition; the B&L overlap effect at human survival is 0.03-1.1%

notes: The finite-window question is settled by the start state, not by the identity: empty start, below mu L T for every finite T; equilibrium start, mu L T for every T. Which start applies at the human-chimp split is M-202 (data-check, open). The arXiv 2208.00148v1 attribution is checked against held text only: the paper is a no-mutation two-allele diffusion (M-223 reads its P_fix(t) -> x0 result), so the 'static and equal to census' condition is the post's own statement, not the paper's. Day's six papers (evo009@L58) are not re-derived here; k != mu is the B branch records. Hancock's 1930s derivation is not in the window.
